meaning.en: Permission or a clear path to go ahead.
meaning.zh: 比喻许可通行或给予方便。

examples.zh: 这个项目终于亮起了绿灯。
examples.en: The project has finally been given the green light.

examples.zh: 为了吸引投资，政府对新企业一路绿灯。
examples.en: To attract investment, the government gave new firms a clear run.

usage.en: Noun; usually 亮绿灯 or 一路绿灯. Borrowed from the traffic signal.
usage.zh: 名词，常说“亮绿灯”“一路绿灯”。比喻交通信号灯。

meaning.en: A person who suffers or takes the blame in place of the real culprit.
meaning.zh: 代人受过或代人受害的人。

examples.zh: 真正的主谋逍遥法外，却拿他当了替死鬼。
examples.en: The real mastermind went free and made him the fall guy.

examples.zh: 我不想给别人当替死鬼。
examples.en: I don't want to be anyone's fall guy.

usage.en: Noun, casual and derogatory; 当替死鬼. In folk belief, a ghost could only be reincarnated by finding a living person to take its place.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，贬义，常说“当替死鬼”。民间传说，鬼要找人代替自己才能投胎。

meaning.en: To mediate in an awkward dispute or situation by saying something conciliatory.
meaning.zh: 在僵局或争执中出面调解，缓和气氛。

examples.zh: 两人争得面红耳赤，幸好老王出来打圆场。
examples.en: The two were arguing heatedly until Lao Wang stepped in to smooth things over.

examples.zh: 场面太尴尬了，主持人赶紧打了个圆场。
examples.en: The moment was so awkward that the host quickly tried to smooth it over.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 打个圆场. Originally from the theatre, where an actor fills the gap with improvised business.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“打个圆场”。本是戏曲用语，指演员临时救场。

meaning.en: To work or operate without a fixed place or routine, moving from one spot to another.
meaning.zh: 比喻没有固定地点或固定方式地工作、活动。

examples.zh: 我们没有办公室，只能在咖啡馆里打游击。
examples.en: We have no office, so we just work from one cafe to another.

examples.zh: 他在几家公司之间打游击，赚点外快。
examples.en: He moonlights around several firms to earn a little extra.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual and often humorous; borrows from guerrilla warfare.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常带戏谑。借自游击战。

meaning.en: To be the first to go into action or take the lead in a task.
meaning.zh: 走在最前面，率先行动。

examples.zh: 遇到难题，老师傅总是第一个打头阵。
examples.en: Faced with a hard problem, the veteran is always first to step up.

examples.zh: 这次比赛由新手小林打头阵。
examples.en: Newcomer Xiao Lin will lead off in this match.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 打头阵 originally meant to lead the front line in battle.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语。本指作战时担任先锋。

meaning.en: To come to nothing; to be ruined or lost.
meaning.zh: 落空，成为泡影。

examples.zh: 一场大雨，我们的野餐计划全泡汤了。
examples.en: A heavy rain ruined our picnic plans.

examples.zh: 他的出国梦就这样泡汤了。
examples.en: And so his dream of going abroad fell through.

usage.en: Verb, casual; the subject is usually a plan or hope. Like something dropped into soup, it is soaked and spoiled.
usage.zh: 动词，口语，主语多是计划、希望。像东西泡在汤里，全完了。

meaning.en: To stop at the crucial point of a story to keep listeners in suspense.
meaning.zh: 讲到关键处故意停下，吊人胃口。

examples.zh: 你快说吧，别再卖关子了。
examples.en: Out with it, and stop keeping us in suspense.

examples.zh: 他故意卖了个关子，等大家追问。
examples.en: He deliberately left us hanging and waited for questions.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 别卖关子. 关子 is the key moment in storytelling, as with storytellers who end a session at a cliffhanger.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“别卖关子”。“关子”指说书中紧要的地方，说书人常在此处停住。

meaning.en: Secret petty moves or schemes to gain an advantage; also fidgeting.
meaning.zh: 背地里使用的不正当小手段，也指无意识的小举动。

examples.zh: 他表面平静，背后却老搞小动作。
examples.en: He looks calm but keeps making petty moves behind the scenes.

examples.zh: 上课时不要做小动作。
examples.en: Don't fidget in class.

usage.en: Noun, casual; 搞/玩/耍小动作. In schools it also means fidgeting.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，常说“搞小动作”。在课堂上也指坐不住的小举动。

meaning.en: Something or someone that obstructs progress.
meaning.zh: 比喻阻碍前进的人或事物。

examples.zh: 骄傲自满是进步的绊脚石。
examples.en: Complacency is a stumbling block to progress.

examples.zh: 这些旧规定成了企业发展的绊脚石。
examples.en: These outdated rules have become a stumbling block for business.

usage.en: Noun, often 成为……的绊脚石; the opposite image is 垫脚石 (stepping stone).
usage.zh: 名词，常说“成为……的绊脚石”。与“垫脚石”相对。

meaning.en: To let one's attention drift; originally, for a soldier to desert.
meaning.zh: 思想不集中；本指士兵私自逃离部队。

examples.zh: 上课别开小差，认真听讲。
examples.en: Don't zone out in class; listen carefully.

examples.zh: 他开会时总爱开小差看手机。
examples.en: He's always zoning out on his phone during meetings.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 差 is read chāi here (an errand). Originally a soldier slipping away from duty; now mostly about attention.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，“差”读 chāi，指差事。本指士兵逃跑，现多指走神。

meaning.en: To waste effort by using an indirect or wrong approach.
meaning.zh: 比喻做事不得法而多费工夫。

examples.zh: 有前人的经验，我们就能少走弯路。
examples.en: With predecessors' experience we can avoid detours.

examples.zh: 创业初期他走了不少弯路。
examples.en: He took many wrong turns in the early days of his business.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; common in 少走弯路 (avoid wasted effort).
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“少走弯路”。

meaning.en: A young married couple.
meaning.zh: 年轻的夫妻。

examples.zh: 隔壁的小两口刚搬进新房。
examples.en: The young couple next door have just moved into a new flat.

examples.zh: 他们小两口感情很好。
examples.en: The two of them are a loving young couple.

usage.en: Noun, casual and affectionate; also written 小两口儿.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，亲切，也写作“小两口儿”。

meaning.en: Something used only as a means to gain entry or advancement, then discarded.
meaning.zh: 比喻用来谋取名利的手段，目的达到后就丢掉。

examples.zh: 他把学历当作进入大公司的敲门砖。
examples.en: He treated his degree as a way of getting a foot in at a big company.

examples.zh: 这份实习只是敲门砖，真正的机会在后面。
examples.en: This internship is merely a door-opener; the real chance comes later.

usage.en: Noun; from the old image of a brick used to knock on a door and thrown away once it opens. Often slightly negative about opportunism.
usage.zh: 名词，原指敲开门后就扔掉的砖头，常略带利用的意味。

meaning.en: Something trivial, simple or childish.
meaning.zh: 比喻不值一提的小事，或幼稚简单的东西。

examples.zh: 这点困难对他来说是小儿科。
examples.en: This bit of trouble is child's play to him.

examples.zh: 你那点本事也太小儿科了。
examples.en: That little skill of yours is really small fry.

usage.en: Noun, casual and often scornful; 小儿科 is literally the paediatrics department.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，常带轻视。本义是医院的儿科。

meaning.en: A weak, cowardly person with no backbone who gives in under pressure.
meaning.zh: 没有骨气、一压就屈服的人。

examples.zh: 敌人再怎么威胁，他也不是软骨头。
examples.en: However much the enemy threatened him, he was no weakling.

examples.zh: 别当软骨头，该坚持的要坚持。
examples.en: Don't be a pushover; stand firm where you should.

usage.en: Noun, derogatory; the opposite is 硬骨头.
usage.zh: 名词，贬义，与“硬骨头”相对。

meaning.en: An innocent person who is blamed and punished for others' wrongdoing.
meaning.zh: 代人受过、承担罪责的人。

examples.zh: 公司想让他当替罪羊，掩盖管理上的问题。
examples.en: The company wanted to make him a scapegoat to hide management problems.

examples.zh: 他不甘心做别人的替罪羊。
examples.en: He refused to be anyone's scapegoat.

usage.en: Noun, derogatory; translated from the biblical scapegoat that bore the sins of the people.
usage.zh: 名词，贬义。译自《圣经》中替人担当罪过的“替罪羊”。

meaning.en: A long-standing fault, bad habit or recurring ailment.
meaning.zh: 长期存在的缺点、坏习惯，或经常复发的病。

examples.zh: 他又犯了老毛病，开会迟到了。
examples.en: He's at his old tricks again and was late for the meeting.

examples.zh: 我的胃病是老毛病了，一累就犯。
examples.en: My stomach trouble is a chronic one that flares up when I'm tired.

usage.en: Noun, casual; usually 犯老毛病 (relapse into an old fault or ailment).
usage.zh: 名词，口语，常说“犯老毛病”。

meaning.en: Unofficial information passed by word of mouth, often unreliable.
meaning.zh: 没有正式来源、私下传播的消息。

examples.zh: 别轻信小道消息，要等公司正式通知。
examples.en: Don't believe rumours; wait for the company's official notice.

examples.zh: 办公室里小道消息满天飞。
examples.en: Office gossip is flying everywhere.

usage.en: Noun, casual; 小道 means a minor path, i.e. an unofficial channel.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，“小道”比喻非官方渠道。

meaning.en: To brag or exaggerate.
meaning.zh: 说大话，夸口。

examples.zh: 他最爱在朋友面前吹牛皮。
examples.en: He loves bragging in front of his friends.

examples.zh: 别吹牛皮了，你根本没去过那儿。
examples.en: Stop boasting; you've never been there.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; also 吹牛. Said to come from inflating ox-hide rafts, which looked big but were hollow.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，也说“吹牛”。相传源于吹气使牛皮筏子鼓起，看着大其实空心。

meaning.en: A serious obstacle in the way of progress.
meaning.zh: 比喻前进道路上的重大障碍。

examples.zh: 资金不足是这个项目的拦路虎。
examples.en: Lack of funds is the main roadblock for this project.

examples.zh: 英语成了他出国留学路上的拦路虎。
examples.en: English became the obstacle on his road to study abroad.

usage.en: Noun; often 遇到拦路虎. Compare 绊脚石, which is a smaller hindrance.
usage.zh: 名词，常说“遇到拦路虎”。与“绊脚石”相比，阻碍更大。

meaning.en: An experienced person who is slick, evasive and hard to move.
meaning.zh: 世故圆滑、不肯卖力、很难被说动的人。

examples.zh: 他是单位里的老油条，什么事都推给别人。
examples.en: He's the office's old dodger and passes everything on to others.

examples.zh: 跟老油条讲道理，根本没用。
examples.en: Reasoning with an old hand like that is useless.

usage.en: Noun, derogatory and casual. Like a fried dough stick that's gone tough and oily, such people can't be shaken.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，贬义。像放久了又韧又油的油条，比喻世故圆滑的人。

meaning.en: A person who is kind and avoids offending anyone, often by not taking a stand.
meaning.zh: 处处与人为善、不愿得罪人，往往不讲原则的人。

equivalents: one who won't rock the boat

examples.zh: 他是出了名的老好人，从不跟人红脸。
examples.en: He's a well-known nice guy who never gets angry with anyone.

examples.zh: 当老好人固然轻松，可有时也要说真话。
examples.en: It's easy to be everybody's friend, but sometimes you must speak the truth.

usage.en: Noun, casual; may be affectionate or mildly critical, since it implies avoiding conflict even at the expense of principle.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，可亲切，也可略带批评，暗含为了不得罪人而不讲原则。

meaning.en: So old that it is out of date and boring.
meaning.zh: 陈旧过时，没有新意。

examples.zh: 这个笑话老掉牙了，我们都听过八百遍了。
examples.en: That joke is ancient; we've heard it eight hundred times.

examples.zh: 他的电脑是台老掉牙的机器。
examples.en: His computer is a hopelessly outdated machine.

usage.en: Adjective phrase, casual; it often modifies nouns with 的. The image is of a very old person whose teeth have fallen out.
usage.zh: 形容词性短语，口语，常加“的”修饰名词。老人牙齿脱落，比喻陈旧。

meaning.en: Unrecorded funds that an organisation or person keeps secretly outside the official accounts.
meaning.zh: 单位或个人私自设立、不入账的资金。

examples.zh: 单位设立小金库是违反财经纪律的。
examples.en: Setting up a slush fund breaks financial discipline.

examples.zh: 他偷偷攒了个小金库，瞒着妻子。
examples.en: He secretly built up a little stash and hid it from his wife.

usage.en: Noun; in official writing it is the standard term for an illicit fund; in daily life it can mean a person's secret savings.
usage.zh: 名词，公文中指违规私设的资金，日常也指个人私房钱。

meaning.en: To do something only as a formality without really meaning it.
meaning.zh: 做事只是形式上应付一下，不认真。

examples.zh: 这次检查只是走过场，不会真的追究。
examples.en: This inspection is only for show and nobody will be held to account.

examples.zh: 开会不能走过场，要解决实际问题。
examples.en: Meetings can't be mere formalities; they must solve real problems.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 走过场 originally meant to walk across the stage in opera as a bit part.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语。本指戏曲中角色从舞台上走过，没有重点戏份。
